trend_gate: at least one named trend or other-architecture Noul at or above threshold

vision_language_action.label: Vision-language-action
vision_language_action.description: A vision-language-action (VLA) or closely related multimodal policy maps visual observations and language instructions to robot actions.

world_action_model.label: World-action models
world_action_model.description: A world-action model predicts future observations, states, or consequences conditioned on candidate robot actions for planning or action selection, or jointly models future dynamics and actions.

agentic_robotics.label: Agentic robotics
agentic_robotics.description: An agentic robot architecture performs autonomous long-horizon reasoning, planning, tool or skill use, reflection, self-improvement, or recovery.

world_model.label: World models
world_model.description: A learned world or dynamics model predicts future observations, states, outcomes, or latent dynamics for planning or control, without necessarily being a coupled world-action model.

generative_action_policy.label: Generative action policies
generative_action_policy.description: The robot policy generates actions or trajectories with diffusion, flow matching, autoregressive generation, or another generative process.

action_expert_modularity.label: Action experts and modularity
action_expert_modularity.description: The architecture separates or composes a semantic vision-language backbone with an action expert, mixture of experts, dual stream, or other specialized policy module.

action_representation_tokenization.label: Action representations and tokenization
action_representation_tokenization.description: The main architecture contribution changes action representations, action tokenization, chunking, discretization, trajectory parameterization, or the prediction horizon.

hierarchical_planning_control.label: Hierarchical planning and control
hierarchical_planning_control.description: The architecture explicitly separates high-level task reasoning or planning from low-level skills, motion generation, or control.

spatial_3d_reasoning.label: Spatial and 3D reasoning
spatial_3d_reasoning.description: The architecture makes explicit 3D, geometric, spatial, point-cloud, depth, scene-graph, or spatial-token reasoning central to action generation.

cross_embodiment_generalist.label: Cross-embodiment generalists
cross_embodiment_generalist.description: The abstract explicitly trains, shares, transfers, or evaluates one learned policy across at least two distinct robot embodiments, morphologies, or platforms. Multiple objects, scenes, tasks, or copies of the same robot platform are not enough.

memory_retrieval.label: Memory and retrieval
memory_retrieval.description: Persistent memory, episodic experience, retrieval, reusable skills, or a failure bank is a central model component.

multisensory_tactile.label: Multisensory and tactile
multisensory_tactile.description: The model architecture fuses tactile, force, audio, proprioceptive, event, or other non-visual sensing with robot decision-making.

critics_verifiers.label: Critics and verifiers
critics_verifiers.description: A dedicated learned critic, verifier, reward/value model, uncertainty estimator, outcome scorer, or failure predictor evaluates proposed or executed behavior.

runtime_adaptation_recovery.label: Runtime adaptation and recovery
runtime_adaptation_recovery.description: The architecture explicitly learns or adapts online from execution feedback, corrects actions at runtime, recovers from failure, or self-improves after rollout.

safety_alignment.label: Safety and alignment
safety_alignment.description: A dedicated architecture component explicitly enforces safety constraints, filters unsafe actions, monitors hazards, or aligns behavior for physical safety. Merely claiming robustness, reliability, or adaptation is not enough.

data_scaling_pretraining.label: Data scaling and pretraining
data_scaling_pretraining.description: The main model contribution explicitly scales or pretrains across large or diverse robot data, human video, simulation, synthetic data, or web data. Ordinary training, one-shot learning, or a small task-specific dataset is not enough.

data_efficient_adaptation.label: Data-efficient adaptation
data_efficient_adaptation.description: The architecture is designed for few-shot, one-demonstration, parameter-efficient, rapid post-training, transfer, or other data-efficient adaptation to new tasks.

efficient_deployment.label: Efficient deployment
efficient_deployment.description: The main architecture contribution targets real-time inference, on-device or edge deployment, compression, sparsity, fewer denoising steps, or lower latency.

other_architecture.label: Other architecture
other_architecture.description: A substantive model-architecture trend not covered by the named hypotheses.

limitations: Jev judged titles and abstracts, not full paper text.
Trend labels describe substantive topics in the title and abstract, not whether a named model was used as a backbone.
Multi-label trend shares overlap and need not sum to 100%.
The default population is scanned papers naming at least one tracked robotics model, so it is not all cs.RO papers.
Other-architecture results require human review because Jev makes typed decisions and does not generate new taxonomy labels.
